::: {.callout-note}
## Known to exist as a class — copies sought
This is a **class of records**, not a single titled publication. Later public sources disagree about whether CSIL was “established” in **1993** or **1994**. The 2008 ministry-commissioned synthesis inspected for this catalogue says only “the 1990's.” Original 1993–95 design, authorization, or pilot instruments have not been recovered. The commissioning issue’s “Continuing Care Division / Community Support Branch” label has not been independently confirmed on a contemporaneous title page.
:::

## Annotation

No Treasury Board minute, ministry circular, pilot evaluation, or 1993–95 program manual was located on gov.bc.ca, openinfo.gov.bc.ca, CanLII, Internet Archive title search, or the Legislative Assembly site in this pass. What exists in public is later description.

The 1993 versus 1994 disagreement is **preserved**. The sources inspected here do not show whether those years name different events (design, authorization, pilot start, first clients) or are simply inconsistent retrospectives. [IFRC’s own pages](ifrc-our-team.qmd) also say Paul Gauthier “started on the CSIL program in 1994” (Anthony Cheng biography) while another IFRC deck uses 1993.

Spalding, Watkins and Williams (June 2006) wrote that CSIL “has been in existence for the past twenty years.” Taken literally that would reach the mid-1980s. That sentence is catalogued as the authors’ wording; it is not used here to move the founding date, and it is not reconciled with 1993/1994.

## Open questions

- Which specific files, memos, Treasury Board or ministry instruments, or pilot evaluations exist and are public.
- What each dated item authorises (design, pilot, or broader availability).
- Whether “Continuing Care Division / Community Support Branch” is the contemporaneous administrative home.
- Access and copyright status for any recovered copies.

## Search leads still worth following

- BC government publications / Legislative Library (1993–95 Ministry of Health annual reports and continuing-care circulars)
- Open Information FOI packages beyond the 2012 briefing note already seen
- CanLII and the BC Gazette for any named CSIL instrument
- Successor Home and Community Care policy-manual revision histories
